surface_geometry_interpretation.definition: In BHSM, surface topography includes gravitational spacetime geometry; it is not limited to a material skin or a separate membrane.
surface_geometry_interpretation.summary: When observations and the admitted model support a gravitational origin, the inferred exterior is interpreted as BHSM spacetime-side surface topography. One Einstein/GHY exterior optical response is counted once; no additional force or mass is introduced and no non-GR residual is required.
surface_geometry_interpretation.evidence_scope: This is a model-conditional interpretation. A fitted or nonrejected light curve alone does not validate a gravitational origin, uniquely verify BHSM or identify a black hole.
surface_geometry_interpretation.unidentified_scope: A unique microscopic interface shape, distinct dynamical surface response, hard-isolation state, horizon and core process require additional physical maps and evidence.

qualifications: Input declarations do not independently validate common-lens association or foreground identity.
Covariance is supplied; Gaussian noise and any cross-epoch independence are declared assumptions. Errors are not rescaled by residuals.
Motion is in the supplied frame; frame, clock and parallax corrections are not invented.
Nonlinearity or noise rejection may reflect parallax, acceleration, association or calibration; it does not exclude a black hole.
This measured-astrometry route is not the only possible future source of track evidence; multi-event association requires a separate likelihood.
No mass, distance, physical transverse speed, horizon, microscopic interface or known-black-hole recovery is inferred.
